body:
Seventh sweep: the unequal-axis path. I chose it because I had raised a question on bd-01KZYBK55CR0T97SE36G9ESPNP and never answered it - the encoding-retrieval section of the introduction builds its cross form by hand and never calls the engine, so I wrote that a reader cannot tell whether the package supports the path or whether the vignette illustrates a concept the package does not execute.

IT EXECUTES. measurement_form has a right argument, and it accepts two relations over DIFFERENT effect spaces:

  encoding relation    3 conditions   word, face, place                  basis encoding:v1
  retrieval relation   4 conditions   word_old, face_old, place_old, lure basis retrieval:v1
  match_control operator              3 x 4

  measurement_form(left = rel_e, right = rel_r, between = edge_frame(...), by = q, over = ov)
    -> effect_measurement_form with a populated block index and readable components

So the capability is real. The vignette is not describing vapourware - it is UNDERSTATING A WORKING FEATURE by demonstrating it with a matrix product the reader could have written themselves.

THE IRONY IS THE FINDING. Forms whose two axes carry independently named bases is the one thing this package does that rsatoolbox, rMVPA and PCM do not. It is the strongest claim in the whole framework. And it is the section of the documentation that shows the least of the package - encoding_profiles %*% t(retrieval_profiles) followed by sum(cross_form * operator), with no relation, no frame, no geometry call anywhere. The one place with no competitor is demonstrated by hand arithmetic.

The fix is now purely a vignette rewrite rather than a feature request, which makes bd-01KZYBK55CR0T97SE36G9ESPNP cheaper and more valuable at the same time.

SCOPE OF WHAT I VERIFIED, stated precisely. I confirmed the form BUILDS and returns readable components. I did NOT check its numbers against an independent hand computation - my attempt failed on my own non-conformable algebra, not on the package. So unlike the symmetric case, where I verified diagonal and off-diagonal blocks to 2.22e-16, the unequal-axis NUMERICS remain unverified by me. Anyone advertising this capability should check them first, and I would not want my 'it executes' read as 'it is correct'.

Seven sweeps, thirty-four findings. Two of the last three sweeps found capabilities that WORK and are undersold rather than defects - the verified unification, and now this. That is a different failure mode from the one this review started on, and arguably a more expensive one: undocumented breakage costs users time, but undocumented capability costs the package its differentiators.
